claims.title: errored skill name resolved by position index, not from the outcome — will misattribute on non-full outcome arrays
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**errored skill name resolved by position index, not from the outcome — will misattribute on non-full outcome arrays**

`allSkills[i]` uses the loop index `i` into `outcomes` as an index into `allSkills`. If `outcomes` is shorter than `allSkills` (e.g., skipped agents don't produce an outcome entry), `i` addresses the wrong skill. The safe pattern — already used by the `skipped` branch — is to carry `skillPath` on the outcome itself and read it there. Using a positional index is a latent misattribution bug.

claims.title: Broad catch in isCliEntrypoint hides unexpected filesystem errors
Test for all-providers-empty / zero-files edge case is absent
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Test for all-providers-empty / zero-files edge case is absent**

The new `runLocalReview` throw path has no test for the `totalAgentsAttempted === 0` case (e.g., an empty file list). Without the `totalAgentsAttempted > 0` guard, that case currently fires the throw with a "0/0" error. Adding a test here would both document the intended behaviour and catch the regression if the guard is added.

claims.title: errored skill-path uses index into `allSkills` but `forEach` index is over `outcomes`
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**errored skill-path uses index into `allSkills` but `forEach` index is over `outcomes`**

`outcomes.forEach((o, i) => { ... errored.push(allSkills[i]?.skillPath ?? "unknown") })` is correct only when `outcomes` and `allSkills` are parallel arrays with identical length and order. If that invariant ever breaks the wrong skill is blamed. A defensive alternative is to have `runAgent` echo back the skill path it ran so the result is self-labelled, but as a minimal fix at least assert the lengths match or use the skill path from the call site directly.

claims.title: Partial-review notice uses `errored` skill paths from the index trick — same misnaming risk
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Partial-review notice uses `errored` skill paths from the index trick — same misnaming risk**

The user-visible PR comment `> ⚠️ **Partial review.**` lists skill names derived from `errored`, which was populated by the potentially misaligned index lookup above. If the index goes wrong, a maintainer sees the wrong skill blamed on the PR, which is actively misleading.

claims.title: Fallback `skillPath` should not default to `"unknown"` — use the skill array directly
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Fallback `skillPath` should not default to `"unknown"` — use the skill array directly**

When an agent errors, `errored.push(allSkills[i]?.skillPath ?? "unknown")` silently degrades to `"unknown"` if `allSkills[i]` is undefined. A PR notice saying `` `unknown` failed to complete `` gives the author no actionable signal. If the index ever goes out of bounds, the bug is in the array alignment rather than the name; the fallback hides it rather than surfacing it. Consider asserting or logging when `allSkills[i]` is missing instead of swallowing it.

claims.title: `isCliEntrypoint` silently returns `false` on any `realpathSync` or `fileURLToPath` error, including permission errors unrelated to the path mismatch
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**`isCliEntrypoint` silently returns `false` on any `realpathSync` or `fileURLToPath` error, including permission errors unrelated to the path mismatch**

The `catch` block returns `false` for _all_ thrown errors, including permission errors on `realpathSync` or an unexpected `TypeError` from `fileURLToPath`. In those cases the CLI would silently become a no-op module instead of the entrypoint. The comment above explains the symlink case, but a broader comment noting that permission errors on `process.argv[1]` will prevent dispatch (and that this is an acceptable trade-off vs crashing at import time) would help a future maintainer understand why `false` is the right default.

claims.text:

**JSDoc comment for agentsSucceeded omits agentsAttempted**

The JSDoc block documents `agentsSucceeded` but has no `@returns`-style entry for `agentsAttempted`. The prose says "callers need this" referring to `agentsSucceeded`, but the parallel counter `agentsAttempted` is undocumented. A future reader must infer its meaning. Add a matching note for `agentsAttempted`.

claims.title: Comment says 'its ${batch.length} file(s) got no real review coverage this batch' but coverage may exist from a prior batch
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Comment says 'its ${batch.length} file(s) got no real review coverage this batch' but coverage may exist from a prior batch**

The error log message says a batch's files "got no real review coverage this batch" — the qualifier "this batch" is accurate, but the phrasing "got no real review coverage" could mislead: files are typically in exactly one batch, so the message reads correctly in practice. However, if a file appears in multiple batches (e.g., a future refactor), the message would be inaccurate. The comment is fine as-is for now, but the wording is tightly coupled to the single-batch-per-file invariant. Low risk, but worth noting if the batching logic ever changes.

claims.title: isCliEntrypoint comment claims realpathSync 'handles the npm-bin case' but silently returns false on any fs error
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**isCliEntrypoint comment claims realpathSync 'handles the npm-bin case' but silently returns false on any fs error**

The comment says `realpathSync` handles the npm-bin symlink case, but the `catch { return false }` means any filesystem error (permissions, ENOENT for a stale symlink, etc.) also silently returns `false` and suppresses `main()`. This is mentioned in the prior review's comment about bundlers, but the actual risk here is simpler: a stale or broken npm-bin symlink at `process.argv[1]` causes the CLI to silently do nothing with no error message, which is worse than the old behavior. The comment should acknowledge this trade-off or the catch should at least log a warning before returning false.

claims.title: Partial review notice for errored agents uses same heading as budget notice, making them visually indistinguishable
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Partial review notice for errored agents uses same heading as budget notice, making them visually indistinguishable**

Both budget-skipped and errored-agent notices render as `> ⚠️ **Partial review.**` / `> ⏱ **Partial review.**` — subtly different emoji, but the same bold heading. The time-budget case uses ⏱ and the error case uses ⚠️, which is correct. However, the body text for the error case says "failed to complete" which is accurate. No code defect, but a low-severity documentation note: the test in `review.test.ts` checks for `"Partial review"` without the emoji, so both notices would match that assertion — if a future test tries to distinguish them by text alone it will be ambiguous. No change needed unless stricter test assertions are desired.

claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Test mock for checkRunsError only guards GET routes but post-change route matching may miss edge cases**

In `buildOctokit`, the mock now checks `route.includes("GET") && route.includes("/check-runs")` to throw `checkRunsError`, and falls through to a separate `route.includes("/check-runs")` branch for non-GET check-run routes. If the real Octokit ever calls a non-GET check-runs route in the path under test, the second branch silently returns `{ data: {} }` which may not match the expected shape and could cause subtle test failures. The guard is correct for current usage but fragile.

claims.title: runLocalReview all-agents-failed guard missing agentsAttempted > 0 condition
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**runLocalReview all-agents-failed guard missing agentsAttempted > 0 condition**

This guard throws when `totalAgentsSucceeded === 0` but doesn't first require `totalAgentsAttempted > 0`. If no agents were attempted (e.g., zero providers authenticated), this produces a misleading error message about "0 authenticated providers (0/0)" even though the `providersRun.length === 0` check right above would have been the correct path. Match the pattern used in `auditRepo` and `runLocalAudit`.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
if (totalAgentsAttempted > 0 && totalAgentsSucceeded === 0) {
```

ENOENT-only silence still hides EACCES/EIO during the realpathSync of import.meta.url
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**ENOENT-only silence still hides EACCES/EIO during the realpathSync of import.meta.url**

The catch now logs everything except `ENOENT`, which is correct for the `invoked` (argv[1]) path. However, `fileURLToPath(new URL(import.meta.url))` is called inside the same `try` block and can also throw (malformed `import.meta.url` in some bundlers produces a `TypeError`, not an `ErrnoException`). A `TypeError` has no `.code`, so `code` will be `undefined`, which is not `"ENOENT"`, so it will be logged — that part is fine. But the comment says ENOENT is "indistinguishable from not the entrypoint" which is only true for the argv[1] `realpathSync` call; a `TypeError` from `fileURLToPath` is a genuine misconfiguration, not a path-mismatch. The log message `"could not resolve invocation path"` will appear for both cases, which is accurate enough to be useful. This is a minor wording/documentation issue rather than a behavioural bug, but the comment should mention that `fileURLToPath` errors also fall through here.

claims.title: New empty-scope test does not assert writeFile was not called
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**New empty-scope test does not assert writeFile was not called**

The test confirms that `runAgent` was not invoked on an empty file set, which is the primary behavioral contract. However, it does not verify that `fs.writeFile` was also not called. A regression that writes an empty or vacuous report on a zero-scope run would pass this test silently — exactly the failure mode this PR is designed to prevent.

Consider adding:
```ts
expect(fs.writeFile).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
```

The restructured block in `review-state.test.ts` wraps the test in `try/finally` with `warn.mockRestore()` in `finally`, which is correct. However, the same pattern in the preceding `it` block (the wrong-shape case, not shown in the diff) still uses the old pattern without `try/finally`. If that adjacent test leaves the spy active after a failure, it can bleed into this test's assertion. This is a minor test-isolation issue rather than a product bug, but it can cause confusing false-positives when tests fail.

claims.text:

**inspect() on null-prototype objects will throw**

The new `inspect(err, { customInspect: false })` branch handles plain objects, but `Object.create(null)` (null-prototype objects) will work fine with `inspect()` — that's actually safe. claims.title: Test assertion on console.error call index is fragile
Comment misstates what `agentsAttempted === 0` means for coverage
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Comment misstates what `agentsAttempted === 0` means for coverage**

The JSDoc added for `agentsAttempted` says:

> "Zero here means a legitimate empty scope (no files matched)"

That is only one of the two ways `agentsAttempted` can be zero. It is also zero when `PROVIDERS` is empty or when every provider fails its auth check before any agent is dispatched. A future maintainer reading the JSDoc will expect the guard `totalAgentsAttempted > 0` to pass through cleanly on an empty file set but may not realise it also passes through on a zero-provider configuration, which is a distinct case and arguably not "legitimate" in the same sense — it may warrant its own diagnostic. The comment should acknowledge both zero-agent causes so the guard's scope is accurately described.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
	/** How many agent calls were dispatched, across every batch. Zero here
	 * means either a legitimate empty scope (no files matched) or that every
	 * provider was skipped before any agent was dispatched (e.g. PROVIDERS is
	 * empty or all auth checks failed). Callers must gate an
	 * `agentsSucceeded === 0` failure check on this being nonzero first, or
	 * an empty-but-valid pass misreports as "every agent failed". */
```

claims.title: isCliEntrypoint error-log comment says ENOENT is 'indistinguishable from not the entrypoint' — this is accurate only for the symlink case
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**isCliEntrypoint error-log comment says ENOENT is 'indistinguishable from not the entrypoint' — this is accurate only for the symlink case**

The comment reads:

> "A missing symlink target (ENOENT) is the one case worth staying quiet about — it's indistinguishable from 'not the entrypoint' from here."

ENOENT on `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` means the file referenced by `argv[1]` does not exist, which in practice means the process was not launched from a real file at all (piped eval, synthetic argv, etc.). That is indeed indistinguishable from 'not the entrypoint', so the comment is correct. However, the comment does not mention that ENOENT on `fileURLToPath(new URL(import.meta.url))` — a malformed `import.meta.url` — would also produce ENOENT and also be silently swallowed. A future maintainer might add a second `realpathSync` call for `import.meta.url` and expect both to be logged on failure; only the first would be. The comment should clarify that ENOENT is suppressed regardless of which path threw it.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: **False positive, verified against the actual implementation.** `outcomes` can never be shorter than `allSkills`: `mapWithConcurrency` (`src/concurrency.ts`) pre-allocates `results = new Array(items.length)` and every worker does `results[i] = await fn(items[i], i)` for every index in range before returning — there's no code path that leaves a slot unassigned. And the call site passes the *same* `allSkills` array both as the `mapWithConcurrency` input and as what `errored.push(allSkills[i]...)` indexes into, so there's no separate-array desync to worry about either. A skipped agent (time budget exceeded) still produces a real `{status: "skipped", skillPath}` outcome at its index — it doesn't skip the iteration.
